Mercator - The Map Maker
 
A Maps codify the miracle of existence. And the man who wrote the codes for the maps we use today was Gerard Mercator, a cobbler’s son born 500 years ago on a muddy floodplain in northern Europe. Mercator was a humble man with a universal vision. In his own time he was ‘the prince of modern geographers’, his depictions of the planet and its regions unsurpassed in accuracy, clarity and consistency. More recently, he was crowned by the American scholar Robert W. Karrow as ‘the first modern, scientific cartographer’. Where his predecessors had adopted a piecemeal approach to cartography, Mercator sought to wrap the world in systematic overlapping maps. Along the way he erected a number of historic milestones. He participated in the naming and mapping of ‘America’, he constructed the two most important globes of the 16th century, and the title of his pioneering ‘modern geography’, the Atlas, became the standard term for a volume of maps. Mercator also devised a new method - ‘a projection’ - of converting the spherical world into a two-dimensional map. Mercator was born in 1512 and died in 1594. His world was one of military conflict, social upheaval, religious revolution - and geographical discovery. He was ten years old when the survivors of the world’s first circumnavigation returned to Spain in their leaking caravel. No better example is required of genius arising from turmoil. He knew poverty, plague, war and persecution. He was imprisoned for his ideas yet patronised by an emperor. His life was one of brilliant breakthroughs and abrupt reversals. In its telling, his is the story of the poor boy made good: the pauper who embraced the world, found fame, faced death, yet triumphed through fortitude. Variously described by his peers as honest, calm, candid, sincere and peaceable, Mercator wore an aura of calm in troubled times. His attitude to his geographical calling was described by his friend and neighbour, William Ghim, as ‘indefatigable’. Some 40 or so of Mercator’s letters have survived, together with examples of virtually all of his printed maps and globes.
 
B Mercator’s most significant work was a project of cosmic proportions. A multi-part cosmography, the work would include a section on astronomy, a chronology of world events and a modern geography, which would eventually contain over 100 maps. Before he commenced the great work, Mercator produced in 1569 an enormous world map on a new projection. His method for converting the spherical globe into a two-dimensional map helped to solve the greatest cartographic riddle of the day: how could the course of a ship following a constant compass bearing be represented as a straight line on a map which had been constructed on a grid of latitude and longitude? Mercator’s solution was to progressively increase the space between his lines of latitude, away from the equator. The effect was to straighten the lines of constant compass bearing (also known as rhumbs or loxodromes). Unfortunately, straightening the rhumbs caused areal distortion: at the map’s northern and southern extremities, the polar regions occupied the full width of the map, while North America appeared to fill half the circumference of the world.
 
C Few of Mercator’s contemporaries understood what he was up to, despite the map’s title explaining that it was intended ‘for use in navigation’. Mercator knew that his projection was unsuitable as an areal description of the world, but it would be several decades before the map’s true navigational value would be recognised. Meanwhile, Mercator was marshalling and editing all the geographical data he needed for his modern regional maps of the world. His sources were wide-ranging and multitudinous, including an imperial physician in Vienna and his competitor, the Viceroy of Holstein. He was still working on these maps when he died. The great cosmography that Mercator had already titled ‘Atlas’ would never be finished. In the Atlas, Mercator had embodied the principles of future mapmaking: his italic lettering, his identical map overlaps, his complete coverage of regions at more than one scale, his consistent use of grids of latitude and longitude, his singular editorial control, were all adopted as cartographic standards. ‘Atlas’, the cosmography, became ‘atlas’, the (Oxford English Dictionary) term for ‘a collection of maps in a volume.’
 
D The projection assumed a life of its own. So powerful a cartographic tool did it become that Mercator the man became subsumed by his own device. By the 20th century, Mercator’s Projection had been adopted by state cartographers to map the land that he had named ‘North America’. In 1938, Mercator’s Projection was selected by the Ordnance Survey to map Britain anew. And in 1974, the American cartographer Alden P. Colvocoresses used the Space Oblique Mercator Projection for the first satellite map of the USA. When the Jet Propulsion Laboratory sent Mariner 8 and Mariner 9 to map Mars, they undertook their Martian cartography on a standard Mercator Projection. One by one, the mappable orbs of our solar system are appearing on the worldwide web, flattened for our screens according to Mercator’s cartographic principles. Mercator’s Projection succeeded in reconciling the sphere and the plane, while his Atlas enveloped the world with an integrated system of maps.

Questions 27-34
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 3?
In boxes 27-34 on your answer sheet, write:

Q27 Cartographers before Mercator had tended to produce separate, individual maps.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q28 Mercator was critical of the work of his contemporaries.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q29 During his life, Mercator experienced great changes of fortune.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q30 Most of Mercator’s published work remains intact today.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q31 Mercator started work on his projection shortly after embarking on his cosmography.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q32 Mercator’s Projection was immediately seen as a major breakthrough.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q33 Mercator produced an accurate area description of the world.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q34 Mercator consulted the work of various people when producing his maps.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

reference:
Q27

干扰 “Piecemeal” 意为零碎的、不成系统的，正好对应题目中的“separate, individual”。

句子 (Paragraph A) “Where his predecessors had adopted a piecemeal approach to cartography, Mercator sought to wrap the world in systematic overlapping maps.”

解析 题目说墨卡托之前的制图师倾向于制作分离的、单独的（separate, individual）地图。原文A段中提到：“Where his predecessors had adopted a piecemeal approach to cartography...（他的前任们采用的是零碎的/逐渐拼凑的制图方法……）”，与之对比的是墨卡托试图用系统的重叠地图包裹世界。Piecemeal approach 对应 separate, individual maps。

Q28

解析 题目说墨卡托批评了（critical of）他同时代人的工作。原文提到他的地图很少被同时代人理解（Few ... understood），也提到了他的竞争对手（competitor），但没有提及墨卡托本人对他们进行过批评，信息缺失，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 文中说了别人不理解他，没说他批评别人。

Q29

解析 题目说在他的一生中，墨卡托经历了命运的巨大变化（great changes of fortune）。原文A段提到：“His life was one of brilliant breakthroughs and abrupt reversals（他的一生充满了辉煌的突破和突然的逆转）”，并列举了他经历贫穷、战争、入狱但又被皇帝赞助，这正是命运的巨大起伏，选 TRUE。

干扰 “Abrupt reversals / poor boy made good / imprisoned yet patronised” 均证明了“great changes of fortune”。

句子 (Paragraph A) “His life was one of brilliant breakthroughs and abrupt reversals.”

Q30

句子 (Paragraph A) “Some 40 or so of Mercator’s letters have survived, together with examples of virtually all of his printed maps and globes.”

解析 题目说墨卡托大部分（Most）的出版作品今天仍然保存完好（remains intact）。原文A段最后一句提到：“...together with examples of virtually all of his printed maps and globes（……以及他几乎所有印刷地图和地球仪的样本都幸存了下来）”。Virtually all（几乎所有）涵盖了Most，survived对应remains intact，选 TRUE。

干扰 “Virtually all ... survived” 强力支持 “Most ... remains intact”。

Q31

解析 题目说墨卡托在开始他的宇宙志（cosmography）之后**不久（shortly after）**就开始研究他的投影法。原文B段提到：“Before he commenced the great work [cosmography], Mercator produced in 1569 an enormous world map on a new projection（在他开始这部伟大著作[宇宙志]之前，墨卡托于1569年制作了一幅采用新投影法的巨大世界地图）”。题目说“之后”，原文说“之前”，时间顺序矛盾，选 FALSE。

干扰 “Before he commenced” 直接反驳了 “shortly after embarking on”。

句子 (Paragraph B) “Before he commenced the great work, Mercator produced in 1569 an enormous world map on a new projection.”

Q32

解析 题目说墨卡托投影法立即（immediately）被视为重大突破。原文C段开头提到：“Few of Mercator’s contemporaries understood what he was up to... it would be several decades before the map’s true navigational value would be recognised（很少有同时代人理解他在做什么……要过几十年，地图真正的航海价值才会被认可）”。Few understood 和 several decades before 反驳了 immediately，选 FALSE。

干扰 “Several decades before... recognised” 反驳了 “immediately seen as a major breakthrough”。

句子 (Paragraph C) “...it would be several decades before the map’s true navigational value would be recognised.”

Q33

解析 题目说墨卡托制作了对世界面积的准确描述（accurate area description）。原文B段末尾提到：“straightening the rhumbs caused areal distortion（拉直等角航线导致了面积变形/失真）”，原文C段也说墨卡托知道他的投影“unsuitable as an areal description（不适合作为面积描述）”，选 FALSE。

干扰 “Areal distortion / unsuitable” 反驳了 “accurate area description”。

句子 (Paragraph B) “Unfortunately, straightening the rhumbs caused areal distortion...”

Q34

干扰 “Sources were ... multitudinous, including ... physician ... competitor” 证明参考了多人。

句子 (Paragraph C) “His sources were wide-ranging and multitudinous, including an imperial physician in Vienna and his competitor...”

解析 题目说墨卡托在制作地图时参考了**多位人士（various people）**的作品。原文C段提到：“His sources were wide-ranging and multitudinous, including an imperial physician... and his competitor...（他的资料来源广泛且繁多，包括一位皇家医生……和他的竞争对手……）”，sources即参考的资料/作品，various people对应physician, competitor等，选 TRUE。

Q35

解析 题目说他试图将地球表现为一张____地图。原文B段（和A段）提到：“converting the spherical globe into a two-dimensional map（将球形地球转换为二维地图）”，填 two-dimensional。

干扰 “Represent the globe as a” 对应 “converting the spherical globe into a”。

句子 (Paragraph B) “His method for converting the spherical globe into a two-dimensional map...”

Q36

解析 题目说船的航线无法在地图上显示为____。原文B段提出了当时的谜题：“how could the course of a ship... be represented as a straight line on a map（船的航线如何能在地图上被表示为一条直线）”，当时的问题就是做不到这一点（could not be shown），墨卡托解决了它。填 straight line。

干扰 题目是描述Problem（解决前），原文是描述Riddle（谜题/目标），对应“straight line”。

句子 (Paragraph B) “...represented as a straight line on a map...”

Q37

句子 (Paragraph B) “Unfortunately, straightening the rhumbs caused areal distortion...”

解析 题目说当墨卡托拉直等角航线时，这产生了____。原文B段提到：“straightening the rhumbs caused areal distortion（拉直等角航线导致了面积变形）”，填 areal distortion。

干扰 “Produced” 对应 “caused”。

Q38

解析 题目说地图的全宽被____占据。原文B段提到：“the polar regions occupied the full width of the map（极地地区占据了地图的全宽）”，填 polar regions。

干扰 “Taken up by” 对应 “occupied”。

句子 (Paragraph B) “...the polar regions occupied the full width of the map...”

Q39

解析 题目说墨卡托最初设计该地图是为了____目的。原文C段提到标题解释了它原本是打算“for use in navigation（用于航海）”，填 navigation。

干扰 “For ... purposes” 对应 “for use in ...”。

句子 (Paragraph C) “...explaining that it was intended ‘for use in navigation’.”

Q40

解析 题目说各种用途，包括由国家制图师绘制____。原文D段提到：“adopted by state cartographers to map the land that he had named ‘North America’（被国家制图师采用来绘制他命名为‘北美’的土地）”，填 North America。

干扰 “Mapping of” 对应 “map the land that he had named”。

句子 (Paragraph D) “...adopted by state cartographers to map the land that he had named ‘North America’.”
